table.description: The viral load set point estimates were obtained from running an automatic procedure implementing an algorithm based on references from Jacques Fellay and discussions among Dr. Fellay and SCHARP. The estimated set point viral load is defined as the average of viral loads within a ?set point window?. The criteria for defining the set point window for a given participant included removing outlying viral loads based on three major categories: values from the initial up- or down-swing of viremia, values from the accelerating phase of the disease, and apparent outlying values during the set point interval. Additionally, participants falling into any of the following categories were excluded from the set point estimation: participants with less than 2 viral load measurements, participants that started antiretroviral treatment within 6 months of enrollment, and participants not yet reaching 6 months from enrollment. The reported viral load set point estimates in this dataset were verified by Li Qin.
